title: The Lesson
brief: Meridian Investigative Academy, final examination. The honor medal has been stolen from the display case in the east lounge. Three people had access. Your task is not to guess — it is to prove. Instructor M. Hayes is observing.
objectives: Identify who took the honor medal — with evidence, not instinct

evidence.label: T-01
evidence.name: Broken Display Lock
evidence.desc: The brass lock was pried with a flat tool — from the inside of the wing, cleanly. No scratches from the corridor side. Whoever opened it stood here calmly, and knew the camera above the case does not record.
interp: Not a break-in. Someone with routine access.
The tool was small. A knife, a ruler, a cleanup scraper.

evidence.label: T-02
evidence.name: Empty Medal Box
evidence.desc: The velvet lining is empty. The box was set back straight, aligned with the shelf edge. Nobody steals in a hurry and then straightens the box.
interp: The thief wanted the theft noticed late — tomorrow, ideally.
Respect for the case suggests familiarity, not malice.

evidence.label: T-03
evidence.name: Muddy Boot Print
evidence.source: Floor beneath the window, east lounge
evidence.desc: A single boot print in dried flower-bed soil. Cleat pattern — athletic tread. Size 44. Someone crossed the flower beds and came in through the gym corridor, not the main doors.
interp: Matches training cleats issued to academy athletes.
The route avoids the main corridor camera.

evidence.label: T-04
evidence.name: Latched Window
evidence.desc: Locked from the inside. The dust on the sill is undisturbed. Nobody came in or out through the window.
interp: Rules out an outsider. Whoever did this was already inside the wing.

evidence.label: T-05
evidence.name: Exam Schedule
evidence.desc: Evening physical assessment in the gym until 20:00. East lounge closed to trainees after 18:00. Only staff, aides and examiners listed for the lounge after six.
interp: Trainees were supposed to be elsewhere — but were they?
The lounge was technically empty and supervised by nobody.

evidence.label: T-06
evidence.name: Torn Envelope
evidence.desc: A torn academy envelope, addressed to D. FOX. Inside: a final warning notice. One more incident and Daniel Fox is expelled.
interp: Daniel Fox had a reason to be desperate this week.
Desperation is a motive — it is still not proof.

evidence.label: T-07
evidence.name: Gym Attendance Sheet
evidence.desc: The evening assessment roster. DANIEL FOX signed out at 18:50 — over an hour before the gym session ended. Nobody signed him back in.
interp: Fox was unaccounted for between 18:50 and the end of the session.
This contradicts any claim of being 'in the gym all evening'.

start.t: Forty years I've kept this place standing. Forty. And in one evening somebody makes a liar out of me.

opts.t: Tell me about the display case.
Did anyone come through here this evening?
Who has access to this wing?

n_case.t: I polished it at six sharp, like every day. Lock was fine. Medal was sitting straight in its box. Everything was fine.

n_ppl.t: The evening class cleared out by eight. After that, nobody came through. Just me and the radiators.

n_keys.t: Staff, the examiner's aides, and the instructors. Trainees steal keys when we're careless — I count mine twice a day.

start.t: I was collating exam papers in the records room. I didn't see anything. I was careful. I'm always careful.

opts.t: Did you pass through the east wing this evening?

n_nerv.t: It's my first exam cycle. If something went wrong on my watch, Instructor Hayes will— can we please just get to the point?

n_saw.t: Around seven I passed Daniel Fox in the corridor by the gym. He said he was heading back to the gym. That's all I know. Please don't involve me in this.

start.t: So you're the one they sent. Great. The screw-up sends the other screw-up.

opts.t: You knew the medal was due back in the vault tonight.

n_gym.t: In the gym. All evening. Until nine. Ask anyone — ask the roster, I don't care.

n_knew.t: Everyone knew. The honor medal goes back to the vault tonight, big ceremony tomorrow, Hayes gives his little speech. So what?

lines.t: WELCOME, INVESTIGATOR.
Sit. Don't fidget. You passed every written test they threw at you, so today we find out if any of it stuck.
The honor medal was stolen from the display case in the east lounge this evening. Three people had routine access. One of them took it.
Rule one. EVIDENCE does not prove guilt. A broken lock proves a broken lock. You will be tempted to treat clues like verdicts. Don't.
Rule two. TESTIMONY is not truth. People lie, forget, or hide things. Sometimes all three in one sentence.
Which is why rule three exists. When a statement and the evidence disagree — you have found a CONTRADICTION. Present the evidence that breaks the story. That is the whole job.

Inspect the lounge. Talk to the three candidates. Compare what they say against what you hold in your hands. CONTEXT decides what a clue means — a footprint is a footprint until you learn who owns the boots.
And rule four: your DECISIONS follow you out of this building. Solve it. I'll be watching.
The east wing smells of floor wax and old paper. The display case stands open like a pulled tooth.

enterEffects: obj:tut|Identify who took the honor medal

phases.title: ACADEMY — EXAM FLOOR

options.label: East Lounge — the scene
options.sub: Inspect the display case and everything around it

options.label: Gym Office
options.sub: The evening class was held here

options.label: Talk — Gus Bloom
options.sub: Caretaker. Polishes the case every day at six.

options.label: Talk — Daniel Fox
options.sub: Fellow trainee. Not your biggest fan.

phases.proceedHint: Hayes expects more than suspicion. Find something that breaks a story: a claim the evidence can destroy.

lines.t: The brass lock has been pried with a flat tool. The scratches run inward — the work was done from inside the wing, calmly.
New evidence: Broken Display Lock.
You check the shelf above: the security camera there has been dead for a month. Its maintenance tag was never countersigned.
Velvet lining, empty. The box was set back perfectly straight, aligned with the shelf edge.
New evidence: Empty Medal Box.
Dried soil, flower-bed dirt. One boot print, cleat tread, size 44. It stops just short of the display case.
New evidence: Muddy Boot Print.
Latched from the inside. The dust on the sill is a flat, unbroken sheet. No entry. No exit.
New evidence: Latched Window.
The exam schedule: evening assessment in the gym until 20:00. The east lounge closed to trainees after 18:00.
New evidence: Exam Schedule.
Coffee cups, paper towels... and a torn envelope addressed to D. FOX. Inside, a final warning notice. One more incident and he's expelled.
Hidden evidence: Torn Envelope.
The evening roster. Most names sign out at 20:00 with the final whistle.
One line is different. DANIEL FOX — signed out 18:50. Nobody signed him back in.
New evidence: Gym Attendance Sheet.
Cleats, cones, whistles. A row of identical academy training bags. Nothing gleams here — the medal is not on the rack.
Locked, and the padlock is Gus's — old, heavy, faithful. You cross it off.

phases.prompt: Present the evidence that destroys Daniel's story.
phases.statement: In the gym. All evening. Until nine. Ask anyone — ask the roster, I don't care.

wrong.t: That proves nothing against his claim. Look at what he said — and what you can disprove.

break.t: You lay the roster on the table. Daniel's eyes drop to the line: FOX — 18:50.
...Okay. I left early. 18:50. I went to the dorms, changed, came back at nine. That's not a crime.
stories change once — maybe. Now show him the floor, Investigator.

phases.prompt: Daniel claims he was never near the lounge. Break it.
phases.statement: I went to the dorms and came back at nine. I never went near the lounge. Not once this evening.

wrong.t: He walked the dorms. Fine. What ties him to THIS room?

break.t: You slide the photograph across: flower-bed soil, cleat tread, size 44.
...That's— you can't prove I touched that case. Nobody can prove it.
When the story changes twice, Investigator, the story was never true. Now make the call.

phases.prompt: Hayes waits, pen ready over the exam record. Who took the honor medal?

options.label: Daniel Fox
options.desc: The roster breaks his alibi. The print puts his boots in the room. The warning letter gives him a reason to panic.

options.label: Gus Bloom
options.desc: He had keys. He was alone. He had access — but the evidence says nothing of the sort.

options.label: Report insufficient evidence
options.desc: Refuse to name anyone yet. Careful — but Hayes did say to solve it.

lines.t: Careful is good. Blind is not.
You hold a roster that says he lied, and a boot print that says he stood there. That is a story with a hole in it. Push on the hole.

completeEffects: remember-hayes|Graduated top of exam cycle; solved the medal case in the right order

lines.t: ...I put it back in my bag before I even knew why I'd done it. The letter said one more strike. One more, and I'm out.
The medal is recovered. Daniel Fox is suspended, not expelled. He'll hate you for a year and thank you in ten.
Evidence first, accusation second. You did it in the right order. That's rarer than you think.
The exam sheet is stamped, filed, and tagged with an old internal number.
One more thing. Your file came through tagged to a training number we retired years ago. 404-C.
Numbers get reused. Forget it.
He says it too fast. He files it too carefully.
TUTORIAL COMPLETE.

completeEffects: remember-gus|Was wrongly accused of theft during the final exam

lines.t: Gus Bloom. Forty years of service, a key chain accounted for to the minute, and boots two sizes too small.
The medal turned up an hour ago. In a training bag. Daniel Fox's.
You had the roster and the print, Investigator. You had the story with the hole in it, and you pressed the wrong spot.
The academy will still graduate you. You'll carry this one instead. Gus will carry it too — that's the part that matters.
The exam sheet is stamped, filed, and tagged with an old internal number: 404-C.
You'll meet worse mistakes than this one. Some of them wear better suits than Fox ever will.
